blocks.text: The opening episode places Elisha’s prophetic work within the pressures of kinship obligations and household economy. The widow’s husband has died, a creditor threatens to take her sons, and her only remaining asset is a pot of oil. Elisha’s questions about what she still possesses and his instruction to sell the multiplied oil therefore address the family’s immediate struggle for survival: the proceeds pay the debt and provide a means for the widow and her sons to live.
